headline: New Mexico took on Meta alone and won a $25 billion judgment over Facebook’s privacy violations
standfirst: A judge on Wednesday ordered Meta to pay New Mexico $25 billion after a jury found the company liable for deceiving users about privacy and content moderation policies on Facebook.
body_markdown:
A judge on Wednesday ordered Meta to pay New Mexico $25 billion after a jury found the company liable for deceiving users about privacy and content moderation policies on Facebook. Judge Francis Mathew handed down the amount, which state Attorney General Raúl Torrez described as “one of the largest, if not the single largest state verdict against a company in American history.” Torrez said the verdict should be a warning for tech companies and that New Mexico would continue to hold them accountable. “This judgement should be a signal, an unambiguous message, to Silicon Valley,” Torrez said at a news conference. (Fortune)

**Business Insider** adds: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg. ROBERTO SCHMIDT / AFP via Getty Images A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion over how it handled its users' data.

**The Verge** adds: Mark Zuckerberg. | Image: Cath Virginia / The Verge, Getty Images The Cambridge Analytica scandal has come back to haunt Meta after a New Mexico judge ordered it to pay $25 billion in penalties for more than 43 million violations of the state's unfair practices law. The ruling marks the biggest legal hit Meta has taken this year, even as it's faced several other losses or settlements.

**The Hill** adds: A judge in New Mexico ordered the technology giant Meta to pay $25 billion after a jury found the company liable for misleading users about its privacy and content policies.

**CBS News** adds: A jury found that the social media company had deceived consumers for years about its data privacy policies.
